components.description: Owns the shared datum 'KV cache blocks'. Compact representation of the doubly linked free queue: free_front (blocks prepended on free, reused first, LIFO), the never-used ids next_fresh .. num_gpu_blocks-1 in id order, then free_tail (cached blocks appended on free, LRU eviction). Block 0 is the null block. ref_cnt lists only blocks whose count is 2 or more: an allocated block not listed has ref_cnt 1, and a block in the free queue has 0. block_hash maps block id to its hash; cached maps hash to the first block holding it.

hash_tokens.description: block id -> prefix length of its partial entry (fine-grained hashes)

components.description: Tagged incidental: create_engine_config returns the config and writes no global (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:2872); `resolved` is the model's hand-off record of that return value, and `current` is restored when the set_current_vllm_config context exits (vllm/config/vllm.py:3467-3469). Scenarios assert on the returned config and the read path.

components.name: VllmIRLoweringPass
components.summary: Lowers vllm.ir ops to the implementation their priority selects.

components.name: s3://vllm-public-assets
components.summary: The public S3 bucket of vLLM test and example assets. Table `objects` holds what the bucket serves, keyed by object key.

components.name: HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient
components.summary: The trainer's control-plane client of the vLLM server's RLHF routes (/start_weight_update, /update_weights, /finish_weight_update); the modeled client records the POSTs it makes and the weight version it finishes with.

components.name: vllm-xpu-kernels (external)
components.summary: The vllm-xpu-kernels package providing torch.ops._xpu_C and the XPU _C ops.

components.name: VocabParallelEmbedding
components.summary: Vocabulary-sharded embedding: each rank looks up its shard and the shards are summed by all-reduce.

components.name: WeightCacheDaemon
components.summary: One daemon per GPU (vllm preload) holding post-quantized, TP-sharded weights and serving CUDA IPC handles to restarting engines over a Unix socket.

components.name: preload health state
components.summary: `vllm preload` weight-cache daemon's /health: 200 once marked ready and no daemon process has exited.

components.name: weight_checksum.py
components.summary: Weight digests and zeroing (owned by models-layers).

components.name: WeightTransferEngine
components.summary: Receives trainer weights for RL weight sync (owned by distributed).

components.name: WeightTransferTrainerFactory
components.summary: Trainer-side registry of weight-transfer engines (nccl, ipc, sparse_nccl, sharded_rdt, m2n); trainer_init builds the engine named by init_info.backend and runs its rendezvous.

components.name: Worker weight-update session flags
components.summary: Worker._weight_update_active and _weight_update_is_draft: one RL weight-update session at a time per worker.

components.name: model_loader/weight_utils.py
components.summary: Hub downloads under a per-model file lock, and building the quantization config from the checkpoint.

components.name: WeightsMapper
components.summary: Renames checkpoint weight names to the vLLM module names (substring, stacked, prefix and suffix rules); a rule mapping to None drops the weight.

components.name: WorkerBase
components.summary: Base worker: KV cache layout negotiation, device sync, model inspection and other RPCs every worker inherits.

components.name: WorkerProc
components.summary: The wrapper process around each rank's worker: its busy loop dequeues RPCs from the broadcast queue, runs them on the worker and enqueues SUCCESS or FAILURE replies.
components.description: Runs in each gpu-worker process; modeled under the engine-core module (where its code lives), so calls into the worker name the rank with on:.

components.name: WorkerProfiler
components.summary: vllm/profiler/wrapper.py WorkerProfiler: the per-worker profiler wrapper with delayed start and a maximum number of recorded steps; start/stop are idempotent, step() advances the counters each worker step.

components.name: WorkerSentinel
components.summary: Fault-tolerance sentinel that executes engine-core FT commands (retry, pause) on the worker; built only with enable_fault_tolerance.

components.name: vllm/v1/worker/utils.py
components.summary: Worker helpers: request_memory (the gpu_memory_utilization budget check) and KV cache bookkeeping.

components.name: WorkerWrapperBase
components.summary: Lazily constructs the worker class named by parallel_config.worker_cls inside each worker process and forwards collective_rpc calls to it.

components.name: WorkspaceManager
components.summary: vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py: the process-wide scratch manager kernels draw temporary buffers from, one slot per (ubatch, lane); locked after warmup so execution never allocates.

components.name: XgrammarBackend
components.summary: Compiles a grammar spec into an xgrammar GrammarMatcher, forwarding the request's stop tokens as override_stop_tokens.

components.name: xgrammar GrammarCompiler (library)
components.summary: The xgrammar library's compiler; only its regex compile time is modeled.

components.name: XgrammarGrammar
components.summary: One request's grammar matcher: accept tokens, fill the next-token bitmask, report termination.
components.description: The matcher itself is the xgrammar library (not vLLM code). It is approximated as a small FSM for a JSON string schema: start -> in_string (after a quote) -> complete (after the closing quote) -> terminated (after a stop token). In each state a stop token is allowed only when the grammar is complete; ordinary content tokens are allowed inside the string. Grammars live in state.grammars keyed by grammar id.

components.name: vllm.platforms.xpu
components.summary: XPU platform module: the torch.accelerator.get_memory_info replacement.

components.name: XPU ops
components.summary: xpu_ops and the torch.ops.vllm.xpu_* custom ops wrapping vllm-xpu-kernels; also Triton selective scan.

components.name: ZmqEventPublisher
components.summary: PUB socket publisher with a replay ROUTER: the scheduler enqueues KV-cache event batches; a background thread numbers them, publishes them and keeps the last buffer_steps for replay.

components.name: ZmqTransport (P2P tier control plane)
components.summary: ZMQ ROUTER/DEALER control transport of the P2P tier; a socket monitor marks a peer connection dead on a fatal event.

scenarios.name: Disaggregated prefill with NIXL: the prefill node keeps the blocks, the decoder pulls them, and the executor reports the receive finished
scenarios.description: The prefill engine finishes the prompt and returns pull parameters (request_finished). The proxy forwards them to the decode engine, whose scheduler asks the connector for external tokens, allocates, records the pull and builds the step's NixlConnectorMetadata. The decode worker handshakes with the prefill engine and READs the blocks; get_finished and the executor's KVOutputAggregator then report the receive finished, which lets the scheduler resume the request. One nixl-pull-connector-scheduler component plays both engines' scheduler roles here.

scenarios.description: Two drafts of k=3 in one step: 3 drafted / 1 accepted and 3 / 3 (metrics.py:33-50). Logging: mean acceptance length 1 + 4/2 = 3, acceptance rate 4/6 = 66.7%, per-position rates [1, 0.5, 0.5] (metrics.py:82-137). Prometheus counters grow by the step's totals (metrics.py:266-281). Accepting more than k is an assertion.

scenarios.name: Drafters handed no requests or zero draft tokens return no drafts
An EAGLE3 decode step verifies 3 drafts in a FULL graph, accepts all plus a bonus token, and proposes the next drafts
At temperature 0 the target accepts the longest prefix of drafts equal to its argmax, so speculative output equals plain greedy output; a -1 placeholder is never accepted
scenarios.description: With the choice `target`, rejection-sampler.sample compares each draft with the stand-in token the target's logits yield at its position (rejection_sampler_utils.py:570-599). Positions 101..104 of a 100-token prompt give 32519, 40438, 48357, 56276. Row a has drafts [32519, 40438, 999]: 2 accepted, then the target's 48357. Row b's drafts all match: 3 plus the bonus 56276. Row c's first draft is a -1 placeholder: no draft is verified and the target's token at 101 is emitted. A plain greedy sample at seq_len 101 gives the same 32519.

The grammar output names the request, so DraftTokensHandler copies the real drafts back (spec_decode/utils.py:84-86).

VLLM_KEEP_ALIVE_ON_ENGINE_DEATH: keep the HTTP server up when the engine core died

VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_CACHE_DIR: local directory the filesystem LoRA resolver plugin serves
VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_HF_REPO_LIST: comma-separated HF repos for the hf-hub LoRA resolver plugin
VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB: the largest audio file run-batch downloads or decodes (MiB)
VLLM_MAX_BAD_WORDS_TOTAL_TOKENS: total bad-word tokens allowed per request.
VLLM_MAX_COMPLETION_PROMPTS: the most prompts one /v1/completions request may carry
VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES: the most sequences (n) one request may ask for; read by SamplingParams._verify_args
VLLM_MAX_NUM_BAD_WORDS: bad words allowed per request by the V2 sampler.
VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS: subtract the profiled CUDA graph memory from the KV cache budget (default on since v0.21.0).
VLLM_OBJECT_STORAGE_SHM_BUFFER_NAME: unset, so the first read generates 'vllm_mm_' + an unpadded url-safe base64 UUID (30 chars) and stores it in os.environ
VLLM_PLUGINS split on ','; unset (null) loads every plugin of a group; endpoint plugins load only when listed
raw VLLM_PORT string; unset -> None; must parse as int
VLLM_RAY_DP_PLACEMENT_NODE_IPS: comma-separated node IPs Ray DP placement groups may use; '' = no restriction
VLLM_RAY_EXTRA_ENV_VAR_PREFIXES_TO_COPY: comma-separated env var prefixes copied to Ray actors on top of the built-in ones
VLLM_RAY_EXTRA_ENV_VARS_TO_COPY: comma-separated individual env var names copied to Ray actors
VLLM_REGEX_COMPILATION_TIMEOUT_S: seconds a regex compile may take (0 disables the guard)
VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING: small-head AITER MLA decode kernel choice (auto | gluon | asm)
VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT: read by rocm_aiter_ops into _SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_ENABLED at import and again by refresh_env_variables().
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER: read by rocm_aiter_ops into _AITER_ENABLED at import and again by refresh_env_variables().
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR: read by rocm_aiter_ops into _CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_ENABLED at import and again by refresh_env_variables().
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS: read by rocm_aiter_ops into _MOE_SHARED_EXPERTS_ENABLED at import and again by refresh_env_variables().
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR: read by rocm_aiter_ops into _LINEAR_ENABLED at import and again by refresh_env_variables().
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA: read by rocm_aiter_ops into _MHA_ENABLED at import and again by refresh_env_variables().
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE: read by rocm_aiter_ops into _FMOE_ENABLED at import and again by refresh_env_variables().
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_ROPE: read by rocm_aiter_ops into _TRITON_ROTARY_EMBED at import and again by refresh_env_variables().
VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE: registers the dev and RL routes (sleep, cache resets, collective_rpc, pause, weight updates)
VLLM_SKIP_P2P_CHECK: the env lambda defaults to '1' (true) although the typed stub says False; true trusts the driver's P2P report instead of the subprocess probe
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE, lower-cased; 'cpu' short-circuits platform detection to the CPU platform
VLLM_TPU_USING_PATHWAYS: true when JAX_PLATFORMS contains 'proxy'
VLLM_USE_AOT_COMPILE: defaults to on with torch >= 2.10 (the CUDA requirements pin torch 2.13) unless the compile cache is disabled.
VLLM_USE_BYTECODE_HOOK: TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper dispatches to the compiled bytecode directly.
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM: allow DeepGEMM where the arch and package support it.
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0: use E8M0 scales when DeepGEMM is used.

VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER: unset means True, so the V2 sampler uses FlashInfer's top-k/top-p sampler on CUDA GPUs that support it (H100 does) whenever a batch is eligible; 0 forces the Triton + Gumbel path
VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM (env, default 0): enables the NCCL symmetric-memory all-reduce op
vllm.__version__ (from the generated _version.py; 'dev' when it is missing); leads VllmConfig.compute_hash's factors
VLLM_VIDEO_LOADER_BACKEND: video loader used when media_io_kwargs names none (reference copy).
VLLM_WATCHDOG_TIME_S = 5.0, a constant in watchdog_loop (not configurable), as ms
raw VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD; unset -> 'fork'; must be spawn or fork
VLLM_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: how long MultiprocExecutor waits for workers to exit before SIGTERM (then 4 s more before SIGKILL)
watermark: fraction of KV blocks kept free when admitting waiting or preempted requests (0 disables it)
watermark_config is set (forces the V2 runner)
weight_transfer_config.backend: None ('' here) means no weight transfer engine
ASSUMPTION: transient activation peak per profiled token for Llama-3.1-8B in bf16 (192 KiB); profile_run measures it with a max_num_batched_tokens dummy batch.
ASSUMPTION: CUDA graph pool memory profile_cudagraph_memory estimates for Llama-3.1-8B (0.5 GiB); the code measures and extrapolates it.
ASSUMPTION: fixed cost of one decode forward (weight reads), ms.
ASSUMPTION: added decode cost per running sequence, microseconds.
ASSUMPTION: CPU kernel-launch overhead of an eager (no CUDA graph) forward, ms; a FULL graph replay avoids it.
ASSUMPTION: the model holds no logits, so a request's natural output length (where it samples EOS) is base + prompt_hash % spread tokens; this is the base.
ASSUMPTION: the spread of the natural output length (see the base); 1 makes every request end after exactly base tokens.
ASSUMPTION: device memory consumed outside the torch allocator by startup (CUDA context, NCCL buffers, cuBLAS workspaces): 1 GiB. memory_profiling measures it; the code has no constant.
ASSUMPTION: launch overhead left by PIECEWISE graphs (attention runs outside the graphs), ms.
ASSUMPTION: forward cost per prefill token (microseconds) for Llama-3.1-8B bf16 on one H100-class GPU, about 18k tokens/s.
ASSUMPTION: cost of page-locking 1 GiB of host memory with xpu_host_register (the code gives no number).

fixtures.summary: Attention's own state: empty backend-selection cache, the modeled backends' capabilities, an empty CPU MLA latent cache.

The MoE world's host as its deployment has it: two visible H100s, so TP 2 passes ParallelConfig's device check (parallel.py:1047-1058). config-platform-seed describes a one-GPU host; this variant overrides its counts in the merged MoE world only.
config-platform's state for merged worlds: the host the platform probes see (one H100 80GB, SM 9.0), matching gpu-memory@rank0 in tp1-llama-8b.

Distributed area seed: a started worker whose TP group follows tensor-parallel-size, on an H100 (sm 9.0) NVLink node with flashinfer installed. Every value equals the components' initial state; it is listed so merged worlds carry it explicitly.
engine-core's starting state for merged worlds: a live client with no requests, an awake executor, a running engine-core process with an async (AsyncLLM) client, a healthy sentinel.

The tp4 world's host as the deployment has it: four visible GPUs, so the TP 4 world size passes ParallelConfig's device check (parallel.py) before engine-core starts the multiproc executor. config-platform-seed describes a one-GPU host; this variant overrides its counts in the merged tp4 world only.

One NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (rank0) serving the FP8 checkpoint neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV (the model vLLM's FP8 tests load) as llama-3-8b-fp8 through `vllm serve` with no --quantization and the default --kv-cache-dtype auto: ModelConfig._verify_quantization takes quant_method fp8 from the checkpoint's quantization_config (Fp8Config: is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized, static activation scales, lm_head unquantized), and auto keeps the KV cache in the model dtype (bfloat16), since only ModelOpt configs name a KV algorithm. max_model_len derives from the checkpoint (8192).
fp8-llama-3-8b with --kv-cache-dtype fp8: the KV cache is stored as fp8_e4m3 (1 byte per element), using the checkpoint's k/v scales.
fp8-llama-3-8b plus every area seed and the areas' variants of it (models-layers-fp8-llama-3-8b, worker-runner-fp8-llama-3-8b).
fp8-llama-3-8b-kv-fp8 plus every area seed and the areas' variants of it (models-layers-fp8-llama-3-8b-kv-fp8, worker-runner-fp8-llama-3-8b-kv-fp8).
moe-mixtral-8x7b-tp2-ep plus every area seed and the areas' variants of it (config-platform-moe-host, models-layers-moe-mixtral-8x7b-tp2-ep, worker-runner-moe-mixtral-8x7b-tp2-ep).
prefix-caching-off plus every area seed.
small-batch-limits plus every area seed.
tp1-llama-8b plus every area seed.
tp4-llama-70b plus every area seed and the areas' variants of it (engine-core-tp4-llama-70b-host).
vl-qwen2-vl-7b plus every area seed and the areas' variants of it (models-layers-vl-qwen2-vl-7b, scheduler-kv-vl-qwen2-vl-7b, worker-runner-vl-qwen2-vl-7b).
kernels-ops state at worker start: CUDA graph capture allowed, no graphs captured, empty compile caches.
tp1-llama-8b plus a rank-16 LoRA adapter for Llama-3.1-8B at /models/lora/sql-adapter.
models-layers in the FP8 world: the FP8 checkpoint loaded on rank0 (Fp8LinearMethod layers, Fp8KVCacheMethod attention with the checkpoint's k/v scales).
models-layers in the FP8 world with --kv-cache-dtype fp8: as models-layers-fp8-llama-3-8b.

models-layers in the Mixtral world: Mixtral-8x7B loaded on rank0 and rank1 (TP 2 + EP: 4 whole experts per rank), its expert layers wrapped by the 2D FusedMoEWithLoRA when LoRA is on; Llama is not loaded.

models-layers' share of the merged worlds: Llama-3.1-8B already loaded on every rank (as load_model leaves it), plus the hub and disk entries the area's scenarios use (Mixtral, an FP8 block checkpoint, LoRA adapters).
models-layers in the Qwen2-VL world: Qwen2-VL-7B loaded on rank0 (vision tower + Qwen2 language model with M-RoPE); Llama is not loaded.

Two NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (rank0, rank1) serving mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 as mixtral-8x7b through `vllm serve --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel`: an MoE checkpoint (num_local_experts 8, num_experts_per_tok 2), so ModelConfig.is_moe is true (get_num_experts() > 0) and FusedMoEParallelConfig gives each rank 4 whole experts (use_ep, ep_size = TP x DP = 2, MoE tp_size 1). max_model_len derives from the checkpoint (32768).
tp1-llama-8b with --no-enable-prefix-caching.
tp1-llama-8b launched with --num-gpu-blocks-override 64: two decoding requests hold 62 of the 63 usable blocks (block 0 is the null block), one free block is left, and chatcmpl-wait-c waits.
tp1-llama-8b after a finished request left the 1024-token system prompt sys-prompt-v1 in the prefix cache: 64 cached blocks with ref_cnt 0, evictable, at the tail of the free queue.
scheduler-kv state for the merged worlds: an empty scheduler and an all-free block pool of the default world's 28,488 blocks (re-initialized by kv-cache-utils.get-kv-cache-configs at startup).

scheduler-kv state for the merged VL world: Scheduler.__init__ sized the encoder compute budget and the encoder cache from Qwen2-VL's largest item, max(max_num_batched_tokens 8192, 16384 image tokens at the processor's default max_pixels 12845056) = 16384 (what scheduler.init-encoder-cache computes).
serving-api's own starting state: a generate model's app state, no stored responses, no LoRA adapters.
tp1-llama-8b with max_num_seqs 2 and max_num_batched_tokens 64, so batching limits show in short scenarios.
One NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (rank0) serving meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as llama-8b through `vllm serve` with no engine-arg overrides (usage context OPENAI_API_SERVER).
Four 80 GB GPUs (rank0..rank3) serving Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct with tensor_parallel_size 4.

One NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (rank0) serving Qwen/Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct as qwen2-vl-7b through `vllm serve` with no multimodal overrides: the checkpoint has a vision_config, so ModelConfig builds a MultiModalConfig (is_multimodal_model) with limit_mm_per_prompt {} (999 items per modality), the lru processor cache at 4 GiB, and the encoder budget defaulting to max_num_batched_tokens (raised to the largest item). M-RoPE positions (mrope_section 16/24/24). The vLLM stop_sign.jpg test image sits in the public-assets bucket; scenarios send it as a data: URL image_url part.

The FP8 checkpoint with --kv-cache-dtype fp8: 1-byte KV elements, 1 MiB per block, 63,633 blocks from the same budget.
Mixtral-8x7B at TP 2: 46.7 GB of weights per rank, 4 KV heads per rank x 32 layers in bf16 = 1 MiB per block, 29,103,380,071 bytes available = 27,755 blocks per rank.
A serving GPU worker after startup: V2 runner, Llama-3.1-8B loaded, KV cache sized (28,488 blocks on an H100 at 0.92), CUDA graphs captured for sizes up to 512.
Qwen2-VL-7B: 16.6 GB of weights, 4 KV heads x 28 layers in bf16 = 896 KiB per block, 59,223,421,543 bytes available = 64,548 blocks.
